walkthroughs.body_html:
Move a wire through a magnetic field and a voltage appears across it. ⚙️

This is the generator effect. If the wire is in a complete circuit, a current flows.

To make the voltage bigger: move faster, use a stronger field, or use more coils.

Use Fleming's right-hand rule (not left!) for generators. Thumb is motion, first finger is field, second finger is the induced current.

An alternator uses slip rings and produces AC — current that reverses each half-turn.

A dynamo uses a split-ring commutator, which flips the connections each half-turn, so the output is DC.

A transformer is two coils wrapped around an iron core. AC in the primary coil makes a changing field, which induces AC in the secondary.

The voltage ratio matches the turns ratio: Vp ÷ Vs = Np ÷ Ns.

A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary. A step-down has fewer. The grid uses both to send power efficiently at high voltage.

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.
Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.
It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.

mcqs.q: What does voltage (potential difference) across a component represent?
options: Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
The energy transferred per unit charge passing through that component.
Voltage is the 'amount of electricity' flowing through the wire.
Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
